title: Drummers as bandleaders
summary: Drummers make good leaders, but leadership depends on personality and taking criticism.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: And would the drummers make better leaders of this?

Well why not? They have a better feel for it, you know. You can see everything around you, you're listening. Everything with leaders has nothing to do with the ability of playing music. I think it's what kind of personality you are. You know, you can make it comfortable, you can make it miserable. You got something like I say, back to that CPA, some of them, a lot of really attitudes, you know. They can make guys fearful before the jobs start. You know, you try to make a person as comfortable as possible. And I've been fortunate throughout the years, because even as a youngster, people did take the time with me and say, hey man, you're not doing it. And don't be afraid if somebody criticizes you. Just go ahead and try to make it better. Take the criticism, especially if it's constructive criticism, and do something right, it's not a put down. A lot of people think, oh, well you just don't like me. I know I can play. Don't tell me. Somebody has to tell you. You have to be able to sit and listen. Whether that's in music or anything, you know. Because music is a funny, funny business. It's a funny business. No business like show business. You have to start to surround yourself. Family have to understand. If you've got more than one in the band, you need an understanding with that. But practice makes it all, especially with drums.
